say.en: Press a doorbell and the sound stops when you let go: no memory. Press a light switch and the light stays on: it remembers. Digital memory starts with two gates that feed each other. In this lesson: Distinguish sequential from combinational circuits.
Explain the SR latch built with NOR gates.
Explain the active-low SR latch built with NAND gates.

title.en: Sequential circuits and the NOR SR latch

body.en: In a sequential circuit the output depends on the present inputs and on the past state, so it needs memory. The basic memory element is the latch, a bistable circuit that stores one bit. Two cross-coupled NOR gates form an *SR latch*: S = 1 sets Q to 1, R = 1 resets Q to 0, S = R = 0 keeps (holds) the previous Q, and S = R = 1 is not allowed because it forces Q = $\bar{Q}$ = 0 and the state after it is unpredictable.

points.en: NOR *latch*: S = 1 sets, R = 1 resets, 00 holds, 11 invalid

narration.en: A sequential circuit remembers its past state. Two cross-coupled NOR gates form an S R latch: set makes Q one, reset makes Q zero, both zero holds, and both one is forbidden.
narration.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮ (ಸೀಕ್ವೆನ್ಶಿಯಲ್) ಮಂಡಲ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡು NOR ಗೇಟ್‌ಗಳಿಂದ SR ಲ್ಯಾಚ್: S = 1 ಸೆಟ್, R = 1 ರೀಸೆಟ್, ಎರಡೂ 0 ಆದರೆ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ, ಎರಡೂ 1 ನಿಷಿದ್ಧ.

say.en: A sequential circuit remembers its past state. Two cross-coupled NOR gates form an S R latch: set makes Q one, reset makes Q zero, both zero holds, and both one is forbidden. Sequential output equals f(inputs, previous state).
say.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮ (ಸೀಕ್ವೆನ್ಶಿಯಲ್) ಮಂಡಲ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡು NOR ಗೇಟ್‌ಗಳಿಂದ SR ಲ್ಯಾಚ್: S equals 1 ಸೆಟ್, R equals 1 ರೀಸೆಟ್, ಎರಡೂ 0 ಆದರೆ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ, ಎರಡೂ 1 ನಿಷಿದ್ಧ.

say.en: Latch: bistable, stores 1 bit.
NOR latch: S equals 1 sets, R equals 1 resets, 00 holds, 11 invalid.
Two NOR gates, each output fed back to an input of the other gate. That feedback is the memory.
Fill the table. S sets Q to 1, R resets it to 0, and with both at 0 the latch keeps what it had.
With S equal to R equal to 1 both outputs become 0, so Q and Q-bar are no longer complements. That is why it is forbidden.

text.en: S = R = 0 holds the last state

say.en: A NAND latch works the same way with active-low inputs: a zero on S-bar sets, a zero on R-bar resets.

say.en: Two cross-coupled NOR gates store one bit. S equals 1 sets Q to 1, R equals 1 resets it to 0, and with S equals R equals 0 the latch holds whatever it had: that is memory. S equals R equals 1 forces both outputs to 0, which is not allowed.

body.en: Two cross-coupled NAND gates also make a latch, but its inputs are *active-low* ($\bar{S}$ and $\bar{R}$). $\bar{S}$ = 0 sets Q = 1, $\bar{R}$ = 0 resets Q = 0, $\bar{S} = \bar{R}$ = 1 holds, and $\bar{S} = \bar{R}$ = 0 is invalid (it forces Q = $\bar{Q}$ = 1). A common use of the latch is a switch debouncer, which removes the extra pulses produced when a mechanical switch bounces.

points.en: S̄ = R̄ = 1: hold; S̄ = R̄ = 0: invalid

narration.en: With NAND gates the inputs are active low: a zero sets or resets. Both inputs high hold the state, and both low is the forbidden case.
narration.kn: NAND ಲ್ಯಾಚ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಇನ್‌ಪುಟ್‌ಗಳು ಸಕ್ರಿಯ-ಕಡಿಮೆ: 0 ಸೆಟ್ ಅಥವಾ ರೀಸೆಟ್ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡೂ 1 ಹಿಂದಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಉಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಎರಡೂ 0 ನಿಷಿದ್ಧ.

say.en: With NAND gates the inputs are active low: a zero sets or resets. Both inputs high hold the state, and both low is the forbidden case. NAND latch inputs are active-low.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A NOR SR latch starts with Q equals 0. The inputs (S, R) are applied in order: (1, 0), (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 0). Find Q after each.
(1, 0): set gives Q equals 1.
(0, 0): hold gives Q stays 1.
(0, 1): reset gives Q equals 0.
(0, 0): hold gives Q stays 0.
So the answer is Q equals 1, 1, 0, 0.

problem.en: Explain why S = R = 1 is not allowed in a NOR SR latch.

steps.en: A NOR output is 0 if any input is 1.
With S = R = 1 both NOR outputs are 0, so Q = Q′ = 0: they are no longer complements.
If S and R then return to 0 together, the final state depends on which gate is faster: it is unpredictable.

answer.en: Q = Q′ = 0, and the next state is unpredictable
